author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Rhode Island entered primary day with a record 37,444 early in-person ballots cast, according to final figures reported Tuesday by Rhode Island Current from the Department of State.

The total, recorded as of 4 p.m., was more than twice the roughly 16,900 early in-person votes cast in the 2022 primary and more than triple the approximately 12,100 recorded in 2024. Rhode Island first offered early in-person voting in 2020 under pandemic-era rules that were later made permanent; just over 7,000 people used the option that year.

The surge came ahead of high-profile Democratic contests, including the gubernatorial rematch between Gov. Dan McKee and Helena Foulkes and the Providence mayoral primary between Brett Smiley and David Morales.

Early voting totals measure how people voted, not which candidates they supported, so the record does not by itself point to an outcome. It does show that a substantially larger share of the electorate chose to vote before Tuesday, a change that can affect campaign strategy, staffing and the pace at which election officials process ballots.
dek: More than 37,000 voters cast ballots before Election Day, more than doubling the state’s previous primary-year benchmark.
headline: Rhode Island primary sets record for early in-person voting
